proof:
The cut-face outward unit normal of $K\cap H_j$ is $-u_j$. Gauss–Green therefore gives
$$
\int_{\partial K}\mathbf1_{H_j}X\cdot n_K\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
=\operatorname{tr}(B)|K\cap H_j|+S_j u_j\cdot[a+B(g_j-y)].
$$
The cut through the interior has no positive-measure coincidence with an old boundary facet, so the common boundary of the two pieces contributes no double count. The same identity in $d=1$ is integration of an affine derivative on a subinterval. Testing translations in the neutrality identity gives $\sum_j\theta_jS_j u_j=0$. The normal matrix has rank $d$, so $\theta_jS_j=c\rho_j$ with $c>0$. The field $x-y$ gives $\sum_j\theta_j |K\cap H_j|=\beta V$, because $u_j\cdot(g_j-y)=0$ on its cutting plane and $d>0$.

For arbitrary $B$, the last identity cancels the trace terms. The remaining condition is $\sum_j\rho_j(g_j-y)u_j^{\mathsf T}=0$. In each coordinate this is a relation of the $u_j$ and hence its coefficient vector is proportional to $(\rho_j)_j$. Thus all $g_j-y$ are the same vector. That vector lies in the kernel of every $u_j^{\mathsf T}$ since the centroids lie on their cutting planes. The normals span, so it is zero.

Because $v_j$ is the only strictly captured vertex, the cut section is the simplex on its $d$ incident edges, at fractions $t_{ji}\in(0,1]$ from $v_j$ toward $v_i$. Its centroid has barycentric coordinate $t_{ji}/d$ at $i\ne j$, giving $t_{ji}=dy_i$ and $r_i=1-dy_i\ge0$. The $r_i$ sum to one. If $\lambda_i(x)$ denote the barycentric functions, the affine margin for cap $j$, scaled to equal one at $v_j$, is
$$
L_j(x)=\frac{\lambda_j(x)}{dy_j}-\sum_i\frac{r_i}{dy_i}\lambda_i(x).
$$
It vanishes at the stated edge cuts and its gradient is a positive multiple of $u_j$. Since $\sum_jr_jL_j=0$, the nonzero coefficient vector $(r_j)_j$ gives a relation among the gradients. They have rank $d$ and a strictly positive relation inherited from the $u_j$. Their unique relation implies $r_j>0$ for every $j$, so all edge fractions are strictly below one.

Now the accepted simplex own-section facet payment lemma 000f61e3347cadf2 applies: all caps strictly isolate their designated vertices, the own centroids are $y$, and the own coarea-weighted normals balance by the translation test. It gives the $q_j$ and $\theta_j$ formulas, and $1/\sum_i(r_i/q_i)=\prod_i(1-r_i)/(1-\sum_i r_i^2)\ge\Gamma_d$, with equality exactly for uniform $r$ in $d\ge2$ and constant $1/2$ in $d=1$. The homothety test identifies $\beta$ with $\sum_j\theta_j q_j=1/\sum_i(r_i/q_i)$. Uniform $r$ gives a centroid source, common edge fractions $d/(d+1)$, and uniform weights. Conversely, those caps have $g_j=y$, and $\sum_j\theta_j S_j u_j=0$ follows from $S_ju_j=dVq_j\nabla L_j$ by the pyramid height formula and the margin relation. The displayed flux identity then gives neutrality at $\beta=\Gamma_d$. In $d=1$ the two normals are opposite, the proper sections are the common point $y$, and the weights $1/2$ give neutrality with $\beta=1/2$ for every interior $y$.
statement:
Let $K=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,\ldots,v_d)$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, of volume $V>0$, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $j=0,\ldots,d$ take the proper caps $H_j=\{x:u_j\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}$ with unit normals. Each $H_j$ contains $v_j$ strictly and no other vertex strictly. Assume the normals span $\mathbb R^d$ with a positive dependence $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=0$, $\rho_j>0$. Let $E_j=K\cap\partial H_j$, $S_j=\mathcal H^{d-1}(E_j)$, and let $g_j$ be its centroid. Use counting measure for $d=1$.

Let $\theta_j>0$ sum to one, $W=\sum_j\theta_j\mathbf1_{H_j}$ on $\partial K$, and $\beta>0$. Suppose that for every affine field $X(x)=a+B(x-y)$,
$$
\int_{\partial K} X(x)\cdot n_K(x)\,[W(x)-\beta]\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)=0.
$$
Then every $g_j=y$ and no cut contains another vertex even on its boundary. With $y_i$ the barycentric coordinates of $y$, put $r_i=1-dy_i>0$ and $q_j=|K\cap H_j|/V$. The cut on edge $v_jv_i$, $i\ne j$, is at fraction $dy_i$ from $v_j$, and
$$
q_j=\prod_{i\ne j}dy_i,\qquad
\theta_j=\frac{r_j/q_j}{\sum_i r_i/q_i},\qquad
\beta=\sum_j\theta_j q_j=\frac{\prod_i(1-r_i)}{1-\sum_i r_i^2}
\ \ge\ \Gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
$$
For $d\ge2$, equality holds exactly when $y$ is the centroid, each cap has section parallel to its opposite facet, and the weights are uniform. For $d=1$, $\beta=1/2$ and any interior mark is consistent with the hypotheses.
title: Affine neutrality of noncanonical vertex caps on a simplex
